overview: This amud is a long list of things a person might see or do in a dream, and what each one means. It opens by finishing an earlier question about an elephant: a saddled one and an unsaddled one mean different things. It then moves through names, religious acts like קריאת שמע and תפילין, plants and fruits, animals, everyday actions, and places, often supporting each meaning with a פסוק or a play on words. Many signs come with a condition, such as a written הספד or a prayer that is not finished. Sometimes the same image means different things depending on its form, its number, or who the dreamer is. Personal stories appear too, from רבי זירא, רב אשי, רב פפא, and רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע. The גמרא resolves a conflict about bloodletting dreams and rejects רב ששת's favorable reading of killing a snake. The amud ends with drinks: all are good signs except wine, which can go either way, though for a תלמיד חכם it is always good.

steps.title: The elephant’s condition makes the difference
steps.stepSummary: The two earlier statements about an elephant in a dream describe different cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: One statement concerns a saddled elephant; the other concerns an unsaddled elephant.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves a difference between two earlier statements. It assigns each statement to a different kind of elephant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier statements can both stand because they do not describe the same sight. The source here gives only the distinction, not the earlier statements themselves.

phrases.english: This one is where it is saddled,
and that one is where it is not saddled.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves two statements on the previous amud by distinguishing their cases.

steps.title: Names in a dream signal miracles
steps.stepSummary: Seeing הונא signals one miracle; seeing one of three other names signals many miracles.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who sees הונא in a dream will have a miracle performed for him. One who sees חנינא, חנניא, or יוחנן will have many miracles performed for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new list of dream signs, beginning with people’s names.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second group receives a stronger prediction than the first. The גמרא states the predictions without explaining why these names carry these meanings.

keyTerms.meaning: הונא, the first name in this dream sign
חנינא, one of the three names in the stronger sign

phrases.english: One who sees Huna in a dream—
a miracle will be performed for him.
Hanina, Hananya, or Yohanan—
many miracles will be performed for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new set of dream signs after the elephant distinction.

steps.title: A written eulogy is a favorable dream sign
steps.stepSummary: A dreamed הֶסְפֵּד indicates mercy and rescue, provided it appeared in writing.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who sees a eulogy in a dream has been shown mercy from heaven and spared. This applies when it is in writing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another dream sign, then immediately limits which version of the dream it means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The favorable reading does not apply to every dreamed הֶסְפֵּד. The final words specify a written one.

phrases.english: One who sees a eulogy in a dream—
from heaven they showed him mercy and spared him.
And this applies when it is in writing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another dream sign, this time with an explicit condition.

steps.title: Answering a sacred phrase in a dream
steps.stepSummary: Answering ״יהא שמיה רבא מברך״ in a dream is linked to עולם הבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who answers, “May His great name be blessed,” is assured that he belongs to עולם הבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns from things seen in dreams to words a person says in a dream.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase the person answers is the important detail in this sign. This statement gives its favorable meaning without adding a condition here.

keyTerms.meaning: may His great name be blessed

phrases.english: One who answers, “May His great name be blessed”—

phrases.aramaic: מוּבְטָח לוֹ שֶׁהוּא בֶּן הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא.
phrases.english: is assured that he belongs to the World-to-Come.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of favorable dream signs.

steps.title: Reciting שמע and the generation’s limitation
steps.stepSummary: Dreaming of reciting קריאת שמע points to personal worthiness, but not to שכינה actually resting upon the person.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who recites קריאת שמע is worthy of the שכינה resting upon him, but his generation is not worthy of that.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a favorable sign and immediately explains why its full result does not occur.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The limitation is about the person’s generation, not the person’s own worthiness. So the statement distinguishes being worthy of שכינה from שכינה actually resting upon him.

phrases.english: One who recites Shema—
is worthy of the Divine Presence resting upon him,
but his generation is not worthy of that.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another dream sign involving recited words, with a limitation.

steps.title: Head תפילין support a sign of greatness
steps.stepSummary: A dream of putting on תפילין predicts greatness; a verse and a teaching identify the relevant תפילין.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who puts on תפילין in a dream should anticipate greatness. A verse speaks of God’s name being called upon a person, and רבי אליעזר הגדול identifies this with the תפילין of the head.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states the dream sign and then brings a verse and a teaching to support it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse describes God’s name being visibly associated with a person. The teaching identifies that description with head תפילין, connecting the verse to the dream sign.

keyTerms.meaning: that are worn on the head

phrases.english: One who puts on phylacteries in a dream—
should anticipate greatness,
as it is stated: “And all the peoples of the earth shall see

phrases.aramaic: כִּי שֵׁם ה׳ נִקְרָא עָלֶיךָ וְגוֹ׳״.
phrases.english: that the name of the Lord is called upon you, etc.”
And it was taught: Rabbi Eliezer the Great says:
These are the phylacteries worn on the head.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the dream-sign list, now supplying textual support.
steps.raayaObject: The favorable prediction for dreaming of putting on תפילין.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The cited verse, read together with רבי אליעזר הגדול’s teaching about head תפילין.

steps.title: A prayer dream is favorable if prayer is unfinished
steps.stepSummary: Dreaming of prayer is a good sign only when the prayer has not ended.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who prays in a dream has a good sign. This applies when he has not finished.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a good sign and then narrows it to an unfinished prayer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The last phrase limits the earlier statement. The passage does not say here that a finished prayer predicts something bad; it simply does not include it in this good sign.

phrases.english: One who prays in a dream—
it is a good sign for him.
And this applies when he did not finish.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another dream of a religious act, this one with a stated condition.

steps.title: A troubling dream image points to understanding
steps.stepSummary: Dreaming of relations with one’s mother is interpreted as a sign of בינה through a similar-sounding word in a verse.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who has relations with his mother in a dream should anticipate understanding, as it is stated: “For if you call for understanding.”
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a set of sexual dream images that it interprets through verses, starting with the word for mother.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The interpretation concerns an image in a dream, not an actual act. It links אִמּוֹ, “his mother,” to the verse’s אִם, “if,” alongside בִּינָה.

phrases.english: One who has relations with his mother in a dream—
should anticipate understanding,
as it is stated: “For if you call for understanding.”

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new group of dream signs whose interpretations draw on verses.

steps.title: Betrothal language connects a dream to תורה
steps.stepSummary: A dream about a betrothed young woman is linked to תורה by rereading a word in a verse.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who has relations with a betrothed young woman should anticipate תורה. The verse calls תורה an inheritance; read that word instead as “betrothed.”
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the next dream interpretation and shows the word change that supports it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse says מוֹרָשָׁה, “inheritance.” The instruction אַל תִּקְרֵי reads it as מְאוֹרָשָׂה, “betrothed,” creating the connection to the dream image.

phrases.english: One who has relations with a betrothed young woman—
should anticipate Torah,
as it is stated: “Moses commanded us Torah,
an inheritance of the congregation of Jacob,”
do not read “inheritance”
but rather “betrothed.”

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the verse-based interpretations of dream images.

steps.title: The verse calls wisdom a sister
steps.stepSummary: A dream about one’s sister is connected to חכמה by a verse that calls wisdom “my sister.”
steps.simpleTranslation: One who has relations with his sister in a dream should anticipate wisdom, as it is stated: “Say to wisdom: You are my sister.”
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another dream interpretation and cites the wording that connects its two parts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the verse states the connection directly: it calls חכמה a sister. As in the preceding cases, the subject is what was seen in a dream, not an actual act.

phrases.english: One who has relations with his sister in a dream—
should anticipate wisdom,
as it is stated: “Say to wisdom: You are my sister.”

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third interpretation in the same group.

steps.title: The final dream sign has two conditions
steps.stepSummary: A dream about a married woman is given a favorable meaning only if the dreamer did not know her or think about her the previous evening.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who has relations with a married woman in a dream is assured that he belongs to עולם הבא. This applies when he did not know her and had not thought about her the previous evening.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the last sign in this group, then limits it to a dream not preceded by knowing or thinking about the woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The closing condition prevents applying the prediction to every such dream. The text requires both that he did not know her and that he had not thought about her the previous evening.

keyTerms.meaning: that he did not know her

steps.whatToRemember: Read each dream sign together with any condition that follows it. Here, both closing conditions matter.

phrases.english: One who has relations with a married woman in a dream—

phrases.aramaic: מוּבְטָח לוֹ שֶׁהוּא בֶּן הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא.
phrases.english: is assured that he belongs to the World-to-Come.
And this applies when he did not know her
and had not thought about her the previous evening.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends this passage’s group of sexual dream images with a conditional sign.

steps.title: Wheat points to peace
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא says that wheat in a dream is a sign of peace.
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone who sees wheat in a dream has seen a sign of peace. The quoted verse mentions both peace and wheat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new dream interpretation and then quotes the verse that supports it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse places שָׁלוֹם and חִטִּים together. That connection supplies the meaning assigned to the dream.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba said:
One who sees wheat in a dream has seen peace,
as it is stated: ‘He makes your borders peaceful;
He satisfies you with the finest wheat.’

steps.title: Barley points to removed sins
steps.stepSummary: A dream of barley is interpreted as a sign that one's sins have been removed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone who sees barley in a dream is told that his sins have departed. The verse says, ‘Your iniquity has departed, and your sin will be atoned for.’
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another plant interpretation and supports it with a verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the link is in the sound of the words: שְׂעוֹרִים recalls סָרוּ עֲוֹנוֹתָיו. The verse supplies the language of removing sin.

phrases.english: One who sees barley in a dream—his sins have departed,
as it is stated: ‘Your iniquity has departed,
and your sin will be atoned for.’

steps.title: רבי זירא waited for a barley dream
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא says he did not move from בבל to ארץ ישראל until he dreamed of barley.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: I did not go up from בבל to ארץ ישראל until I saw barley in a dream.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא adds a personal account immediately after the barley interpretation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His account shows that the barley dream mattered to him before his move. The text does not give a further reason for his wait.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:

phrases.aramaic: אֲנָא לָא סְלַקִי מִבָּבֶל לְאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל
phrases.english: I did not go up from Babylonia to the Land of Israel
until I saw barley in a dream.

steps.title: A laden vine points to a healthy pregnancy
steps.stepSummary: A vine heavy with fruit is interpreted as a sign that the dreamer's wife will not miscarry.
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone who sees a laden vine in a dream—his wife will not miscarry. The verse compares a wife to a fruitful vine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to vines and gives the first vine interpretation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The dream shows a vine bearing fruit. The quoted verse connects a fruitful vine with one's wife.

phrases.english: One who sees a laden vine in a dream—
his wife will not miscarry,
as it is stated: ‘Your wife shall be like a fruitful vine.’

steps.title: A choice vine points toward משיח
steps.stepSummary: Seeing a שׂוֹרֵקָה is interpreted as a reason to anticipate משיח.
steps.simpleTranslation: For a choice vine, one should anticipate משיח. The quoted verse mentions both a vine and a choice vine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, different vine image and its interpretation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier case was a laden vine; this one names a שׂוֹרֵקָה. Its supporting verse is part of the blessing associated with the future ruler.

phrases.english: A choice vine—he should anticipate the Messiah,
as it is stated: ‘Binding his foal to the vine
and his donkey's colt to the choice vine.’

steps.title: A fig points to retained תורה
steps.stepSummary: A fig seen in a dream is interpreted as a sign that the dreamer's תורה stays with him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone who sees a fig in a dream—his learning is preserved within him. The verse says that one who tends a fig tree will eat its fruit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns from vines to a fig and gives its meaning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse describes keeping or tending a fig tree and receiving its fruit. The interpretation applies that image of keeping to retaining תורה.

phrases.english: One who sees a fig in a dream—
his Torah learning is preserved within him,
as it is stated: ‘One who tends a fig tree
will eat its fruit.’

steps.title: Pomegranate size points to business growth
steps.stepSummary: Small and large pomegranates each point to success in business, with a different description of that success.
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone who sees pomegranates in a dream: if they are small, his business will flourish like a pomegranate; if they are large, his business will grow like a pomegranate.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a set of pomegranate cases by distinguishing small fruit from large fruit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both cases concern business. The wording changes from flourishing in the small-fruit case to growing in the large-fruit case.

phrases.english: One who sees pomegranates in a dream, if they are small—
his business flourishes like a pomegranate;
if they are large—his business grows like a pomegranate.

steps.title: Split pomegranates for a תלמיד חכם
steps.stepSummary: For a תלמיד חכם, split pomegranates point to more תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the pomegranates are split and the dreamer is a תלמיד חכם, he should anticipate תורה. The verse speaks of pomegranate juice.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא changes the pomegranate case: now the fruit is split, and the dreamer's identity matters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This first branch concerns a תלמיד חכם. The quoted verse supplies the pomegranate image used for the תורה interpretation.

phrases.english: If they are split, and he is a Torah scholar—
he should anticipate Torah,
as it is stated: ‘I would give you spiced wine to drink,
from the juice of my pomegranate.’

steps.title: Split pomegranates for an עם הארץ
steps.stepSummary: For an עם הארץ, split pomegranates point to מצוות rather than the outcome just given for a תלמיד חכם.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he is an עם הארץ, he should anticipate מצוות. The verse compares the temple of the head to a split pomegranate.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the other branch of the split-pomegranate case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fruit is still split, but the dreamer is now an עם הארץ. The next lines will explain how the verse supports the מצוות interpretation.

keyTerms.meaning: your temple, at the side of the head

phrases.english: And if he is an unlearned person—
he should anticipate מצוות,
as it is stated: ‘Your temple is like a slice of pomegranate.’

steps.title: What does the verse's word suggest?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how to understand רַקָּתֵךְ in the quoted verse.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does ‘your temple’ mean here?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses over one word in the verse to set up its explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous step quoted a comparison to a pomegranate. This question draws attention to the particular word that will connect the verse to an עם הארץ.

keyTerms.meaning: people regarded as empty; the word used in the coming explanation

phrases.english: What is the meaning of ‘your temple’?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the word רַקָּתֵךְ supports the interpretation about מצוות.

steps.title: Even those called empty are full of מצוות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads רַקָּתֵךְ as pointing to רֵיקָנִין, who are nevertheless full of מצוות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even the seemingly empty people among you are full of מצוות like a pomegranate.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its word question and completes the explanation of the עם הארץ case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It links רַקָּתֵךְ to the similar-sounding רֵיקָנִין. The pomegranate image then expresses how full of מצוות even these people are.

phrases.english: Even the seemingly empty people among you
are full of מצוות like a pomegranate.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רַקָּתֵךְ is read as an allusion to רֵיקָנִין, who are full of מצוות.

steps.title: Small olives point to lasting business growth
steps.stepSummary: Small olives in a dream point to a business that flourishes, grows, and lasts.
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone who sees small olives in a dream—his business will flourish, grow, and endure like olives.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves from pomegranates to olives and begins with small olives.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This interpretation concerns business, as the small-pomegranate case did. Here the text adds that the business will also endure.

phrases.english: One who sees olives in a dream, if they are small—
his business flourishes, grows, and endures like olives.

steps.title: Olive fruit and olive trees mean different things
steps.stepSummary: The business interpretation applies to olive fruit; olive trees instead point to many children.
steps.simpleTranslation: That applies to the fruit. But if he sees olive trees, he will have many children, as the verse says, ‘Your children are like olive saplings,’ and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows the previous interpretation and adds a separate one for olive trees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The distinction is between fruit and tree. The verse explicitly compares children to olive saplings, supporting the tree interpretation.

phrases.english: And this applies to fruit,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל אִילָנֵי — הָוְיִין לֵיהּ בָּנִים מְרוּבִּין,
phrases.english: but for trees—he will have many children,
as it is stated: ‘Your children are like olive saplings,’ and so on.

steps.title: Another interpretation of an olive tree
steps.stepSummary: A second reported interpretation says that seeing an olive tree points to a good reputation.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say that one who sees an olive tree in a dream will gain a good name. The verse says that God called your name a flourishing olive tree, beautiful in fruit and form.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports another view of what an olive tree in a dream means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The preceding interpretation connected olive trees to children. This reported view instead uses a verse that calls the olive tree by a name to support a good reputation.

phrases.english: Some say: One who sees an olive tree in a dream—
a good reputation will spread for him,
as it is stated: ‘A flourishing olive tree, beautiful in fruit and form,
the Lord called your name.’

steps.title: Olive oil points to the light of תורה
steps.stepSummary: Olive oil in a dream is interpreted as a sign to anticipate the light of תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone who sees olive oil in a dream should anticipate the light of תורה, as the verse says, ‘They shall bring you pure olive oil.’
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a separate interpretation for olive oil, rather than olives or olive trees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse names olive oil used for light. That gives the interpretation its link between oil, light, and תורה.

phrases.english: One who sees olive oil in a dream—
he should anticipate the light of Torah,
as it is stated: ‘They shall bring to you
pure olive oil.’

steps.title: Dates point to sins coming to an end
steps.stepSummary: Dates in a dream are interpreted as a sign that the dreamer's sins have ended.
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone who sees dates in a dream—his sins have come to an end. The verse says, ‘Your iniquity has ended, daughter of Zion.’
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives an interpretation for dates, the last of the fruit signs in this run before it turns to רב יוסף's teachings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The connection rests on the similar sound of תְּמָרִים and תַּמּוּ. Like the earlier barley case, the outcome concerns sins, but this interpretation uses the language of an ending.

phrases.english: One who sees dates in a dream—
his sins have ended,
as it is stated: ‘Your iniquity has ended, daughter of Zion.’

steps.whatToRemember: Across this list, watch what changes: sometimes a different plant gives a new meaning, and sometimes the same plant gives different meanings depending on its form or on who dreamed it.

steps.title: One goat points to one blessed year; several goats point to several
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף distinguishes between seeing one goat and seeing several goats in a dream.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף says that a goat in a dream points to a blessed year, while goats point to blessed years. He cites a verse about goats’ milk providing food.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new dream sign and supports it with a verse. The number of goats changes the number of blessed years.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse connects goats with a continuing supply of food. The interpretation applies that image of plenty to the dreamer’s years.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף, הָרוֹאֶה עֵז בַּחֲלוֹם
phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: One who sees a goat in a dream
— a year will be blessed for him,
goats — years will be blessed for him,
as it is stated: “And enough goats’ milk for your food.”

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף, הָרוֹאֶה עֵז בַּחֲלוֹם
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A goat signals one blessed year; goats signal blessed years.

steps.title: Myrtle points to successful property or an inheritance
steps.stepSummary: Seeing הדס signals success for existing property, or an inheritance if the dreamer has none.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who sees myrtle in a dream will have success with his property. If he has no property, an inheritance will come to him from elsewhere.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives two outcomes for the same dream sign. Which outcome applies depends on whether the dreamer already has property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Property he owns can prosper. If he owns none, the positive outcome takes the form of property coming to him.

phrases.english: One who sees myrtle in a dream
— his property will prosper for him.
And if he has no property
— an inheritance will come to him from elsewhere.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: A dream of הדס signals property prospering, or an inheritance for someone without property.

steps.title: The myrtle sign requires seeing it on its stem
steps.stepSummary: An attributed teaching limits the preceding הדס interpretation to a particular way of seeing it.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said—and some say it was taught in a teaching—that this applies when he sees the myrtle on its stems.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא qualifies the preceding הדס sign. It also gives two possible attributions for this qualification.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier promise does not apply to every sight of הדס. This line specifies that the dreamer must see it on its stems.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר עוּלָּא, וְאָמְרִי לַהּ בְּמַתְנִיתָא תָּנָא:
phrases.english: Ulla said, and some say it was taught in a teaching:
And that is when he saw them on their stems.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר עוּלָּא, וְאָמְרִי לַהּ בְּמַתְנִיתָא תָּנָא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The preceding הדס interpretation applies when it is seen on its stems.

steps.title: A citron points to being honored before one’s Creator
steps.stepSummary: The dream interpretation connects אתרוג with the verse’s word הָדָר.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who sees a citron in a dream is honored before his Creator, as the verse says: “Fruit of a splendid tree, branches of palm trees.”
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new dream sign. It uses a verse describing the fruit as הָדָר to explain the favorable interpretation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse supplies the word הָדָר, meaning splendid or honored. The interpretation applies that word to the dreamer’s standing before his Creator.

phrases.english: One who sees a citron in a dream
— he is honored before his Creator,
as it is stated: “Fruit of a splendid tree, branches of palm trees.”

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Seeing an אתרוג indicates being הָדוּר before one’s Creator.

steps.title: A palm branch points to a heart devoted to Heaven
steps.stepSummary: Seeing לולב signals wholehearted devotion to the dreamer’s Father in Heaven.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who sees a palm branch in a dream has only one heart for his Father in Heaven.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another dream interpretation, now for לולב. It describes the dreamer as having one heart directed toward Heaven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the preceding אתרוג sign, this line does not quote a verse. Its focus is the dreamer’s single-hearted devotion.

phrases.english: One who sees a palm branch in a dream
— has only one heart
for his Father in Heaven.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: A dream of לולב signals a heart devoted to Heaven.

steps.title: A goose points to wisdom
steps.stepSummary: Seeing a goose is interpreted as a reason to expect wisdom.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who sees a goose in a dream should anticipate wisdom, as it is stated: “Wisdoms cry out in the street.”
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא introduces a goose as a new dream sign and cites a verse about wisdom calling aloud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The quoted verse supplies an image of wisdom raising its voice. The interpretation links that image to the goose.

phrases.english: One who sees a goose in a dream
— should anticipate wisdom,
as it is stated: “Wisdoms cry out in the street.”

steps.mimraCoreRuling: A goose in a dream signals that one should anticipate wisdom.

steps.title: A further goose dream points to leading a yeshiva
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a second, more specific interpretation involving the goose.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who has relations with it in the dream becomes ראש ישיבה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds another goose-dream case. It assigns this case the specific outcome of becoming ראש ישיבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first goose case concerned seeing it and anticipating wisdom. This case describes a different dream action and a different predicted outcome.

keyTerms.meaning: one who has relations with it

phrases.english: And one who has relations with it
becomes head of a yeshiva.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Having relations with the goose in the dream signals becoming ראש ישיבה.

steps.title: רב אשי reports that the goose dream came true for him
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי relates his own dream and subsequent rise to greatness.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: I saw it, had relations with it, and rose to greatness.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי adds a personal account after the goose interpretation. He says he had that dream and later rose to greatness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His account connects the preceding dream case with his own experience. It does not introduce a new condition for interpreting the dream.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: I saw it,
and had relations with it, and rose to greatness.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב אשי reports that the preceding goose-dream case was followed by his rise to greatness.

steps.title: Roosters and a hen point to different good outcomes
steps.stepSummary: One rooster points to one son, several roosters to sons, and a hen to a beautiful garden and joy.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who sees a rooster in a dream should anticipate a male child; roosters, male children; a hen, a beautiful garden and joy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא lists three related bird-dream signs. It distinguishes a single rooster, multiple roosters, and a hen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: As with the goats, singular and plural change the number of children expected. The hen receives a different interpretation altogether.

phrases.english: One who sees a rooster in a dream
— should anticipate a male child.
Roosters — he should anticipate male children.
A hen — he should anticipate a beautiful garden and joy.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: The rooster, roosters, and hen each have the stated dream interpretation.

steps.title: Eggs point to a pending request; broken eggs to its fulfillment
steps.stepSummary: The condition of the eggs changes the interpretation of the dreamer’s request.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who sees eggs in a dream has a request that is pending. If they break, his request has been fulfilled.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא introduces eggs as a dream sign, then immediately distinguishes intact eggs from broken ones.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Seeing eggs means the request remains unresolved. Seeing them break means the request has been granted.

phrases.english: One who sees eggs in a dream
— his request is pending.
If they broke — his request has been fulfilled.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Eggs signal a pending request; broken eggs signal its fulfillment.

steps.title: The broken-object sign extends beyond eggs
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא applies the preceding pattern to nuts, cucumbers, glass vessels, and similar breakable things.
steps.simpleTranslation: The same applies to nuts, cucumbers, all glass vessels, and other things that break like these.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא extends the egg interpretation to a list of other objects. This line completes the preceding dream-sign rule rather than starting an unrelated one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For these objects too, seeing them broken points to the request being fulfilled. The list ends by including other similarly breakable things.

phrases.english: And likewise nuts, and likewise cucumbers,
and likewise all glass vessels,
and likewise all things that break like these.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: The preceding broken-object interpretation also applies to the listed objects and similar ones.

steps.title: Entering a city points to fulfilled wishes
steps.stepSummary: A dream of entering a city is linked to a verse about reaching a desired destination.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who enters a city will have his wishes fulfilled, as it is stated: “And He led them to their desired haven.”
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to another dream scene and supports its interpretation with a verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse describes arriving at the place one wanted to reach. The dream interpretation applies that arrival to the dreamer’s wishes.

phrases.english: One who enters a city
— his wishes have been fulfilled for him,
as it is stated: “And He led them to their desired haven.”

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Entering a city in a dream signals fulfilled wishes.

steps.title: Shaving the head is a good sign, and shaving the beard extends it to the family
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא distinguishes shaving the head alone from shaving both head and beard in a dream.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who shaves his head in a dream has a good sign for himself. If he shaves his head and beard, the good sign is for him and his whole family.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another dream interpretation. Adding the beard broadens who benefits from the good sign.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the head alone, the sign is for the dreamer. With both head and beard, it includes his entire family.
steps.whatToRemember: In this last group of signs, a small change in the dream scene can change the interpretation: one or several, intact or broken, head alone or head and beard.

phrases.english: One who shaves his head in a dream
— it is a good sign for him.
His head and his beard
— for him and for his entire family.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Shaving the head is a good sign for the dreamer; shaving head and beard is a good sign for the whole family.

steps.title: The size and position of a boat
steps.stepSummary: A small boat points to a good name for the dreamer; a large boat extends that good name to the family. The sign applies when the boat is riding high.
steps.simpleTranslation: Sitting in a small boat means a good name will spread for him. In a large boat, it will spread for him and his whole family—but only if the boat is riding high.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a boat-dream sign, then limits when that sign applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Boat size changes who shares in the good name. The final line adds a separate condition: the boat must be high in the water.

phrases.english: One who sits in a small boat—
a good name spreads for him.
In a large boat—
for him and his entire family.
And this applies when it is riding high.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of dream signs with a new image.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A boat riding high signals a good name; its size determines whether that sign extends to the family.

steps.title: A good sign with a condition
steps.stepSummary: Relieving oneself in a dream is a good sign, supported by a verse, provided the dream does not include wiping.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who relieves himself in a dream has a good sign, as the verse says, “The one who is bent down will quickly be released.” This applies when he did not wipe.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new dream sign, quotes a verse for it, and immediately states a condition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse connects the dream image with release. The final phrase limits the favorable reading to a dream without wiping.

keyTerms.meaning: the bent-down one will quickly be released

phrases.english: One who relieves himself in a dream—
it is a favorable sign for him, as it is stated:
“The bent-down one will quickly be released.”
And this applies when he did not wipe.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the boat dream to a different dream image, again with a limiting condition.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Relieving oneself in a dream is favorable if the dream does not include wiping.

steps.title: Going up and down from a roof
steps.stepSummary: Going up to a roof signals rising to greatness; coming down signals losing that greatness.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who goes up to a roof in a dream rises to greatness. If he comes down, he descends from his greatness.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא first gives opposite readings for going up and coming down. This sets up the different reading in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first reading treats each direction as meaningful: upward means a rise, and downward means a fall. אביי and רבא will then address whether the downward part can undo the upward sign.

keyTerms.meaning: one who goes up to the roof

phrases.english: One who goes up to the roof in a dream—
rises to greatness.
If he came down—he descends from his greatness.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces a new dream sign based on movement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The initial reading assigns opposite outcomes to climbing up and coming down.

steps.title: The rise remains in place
steps.stepSummary: אביי and רבא say that once the dreamer has gone up, the rise remains meaningful.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי and רבא both said: Once he has gone up, he has gone up.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי and רבא push back on the idea that coming down cancels the favorable sign of going up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous line read the descent as a loss of greatness. Their statement keeps the ascent decisive even if the dream later includes a descent.

phrases.english: Abaye and Rava both said:
Once he has gone up—he has gone up.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Qualifies the previous step’s reading of coming down.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that a later descent undoes the sign of having ascended.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It gives the later descent too much power over the earlier ascent.

steps.title: Torn clothing and a torn decree
steps.stepSummary: Tearing clothing in a dream signals that the dreamer’s decree is torn up.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who tears his clothes in a dream: they tear up his decree.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new dream sign, matching the tearing in the dream to a favorable result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The dreamer tears clothing; the sign is that his decree is torn instead. There is no added condition in this line.

phrases.english: One who tears his clothes in a dream—
they tear up his decree.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the roof discussion and introduces another dream image.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Tearing one’s clothes in a dream signals the tearing up of one’s decree.

steps.title: The place changes the sign of nakedness
steps.stepSummary: Standing naked in a dream has opposite readings in בבל and ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who stands naked in a dream: in בבל, he stands without sin; in ארץ ישראל, he is naked of מצוות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives one dream image but two outcomes, depending on where the dreamer is standing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In בבל, nakedness is read as being without sin. In ארץ ישראל, the same nakedness is read as lacking מצוות; the location changes the interpretation.

phrases.english: One who stands naked in a dream,
in Babylonia—stands without sin.
In the Land of Israel—he is naked without מצוות.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a new sign whose meaning depends on location.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The place seen in the dream determines whether nakedness points to freedom from sin or lack of מצוות.

steps.title: Being held can signal protection
steps.stepSummary: Being seized by a soldier signals protection; a neck chain signals added protection. An ordinary rope does not carry the neck-chain sign.
steps.simpleTranslation: One seized by a soldier receives protection. If they put him in a neck chain, they add protection to his protection. This applies to a neck chain, but not to an ordinary rope.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives two levels of a protection sign, then limits the stronger sign to a neck chain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being seized points to protection, and being placed in a neck chain points to more protection. The final line says not to give that neck-chain reading to a mere rope.

phrases.english: One who is seized by a soldier—
protection is provided for him.
If they placed him in a neck chain—
they added protection to his protection.
And this applies to a neck chain,
but not to an ordinary rope.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new dream image and distinguishes its precise details.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Seizure by a soldier signals protection; a neck chain signals added protection, unlike an ordinary rope.

steps.title: A marsh and a forest point to different leaders
steps.stepSummary: Entering a marsh signals becoming a ראש ישיבה; entering a forest signals becoming a leader of בני כלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who enters a marsh in a dream becomes ראש ישיבה. One who enters a forest becomes head of the בני כלה, the advanced students.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives two similar dreams with different leadership outcomes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The difference is the setting: a marsh points to ראש ישיבה, while a forest points to leadership of בני כלה. The text names the two outcomes without explaining the image further here.

phrases.english: One who enters a marsh in a dream—
becomes head of a yeshiva.
If he enters a forest—
he becomes head of the advanced students.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins another paired set of dream signs, this time contrasting two settings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A marsh and a forest point to two different leadership roles.

steps.title: Two dreams point to different leadership roles
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא dreams of entering a marsh and becomes a ראש ישיבה; רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע dreams of entering a forest and becomes head of בני כלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא and רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע each had a dream. Entering a marsh was followed by appointment as ראש ישיבה; entering a forest was followed by appointment as head of בני כלה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives examples of the two dream signs just introduced. Each dream is followed by a different leadership appointment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This account distinguishes the men by where they went in the dream. The marsh goes with ראש ישיבה, while the forest goes with leadership of בני כלה.

phrases.aramaic: רַב פָּפָּא וְרַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ חֲזוֹ חֶלְמָא:
phrases.english: Rav Pappa and Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua saw a dream:

phrases.aramaic: רַב פָּפָּא דְּעָיֵיל לְאַגְמָא — נַעֲשָׂה רֹאשׁ יְשִׁיבָה.
phrases.english: Rav Pappa, who entered a marsh, became head of a yeshiva.

phrases.aramaic: רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ דְּעָיֵיל לְיַעַר —
phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua, who entered a forest—
became head of the advanced students.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא וְרַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ חֲזוֹ חֶלְמָא:
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides named examples of the two leadership signs stated in step 48.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The marsh and forest dreams correspond to different leadership appointments.

steps.title: Another account distinguishes the dreams by a hanging drum
steps.stepSummary: An alternate account says both men entered a marsh; only רב פפא had a hanging drum in his dream.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say both entered a marsh. רב פפא had a hanging drum and became ראש ישיבה; רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע did not have one and became head of בני כלה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another version of the story. It now uses the drum, rather than marsh versus forest, to distinguish the two appointments.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, entering a marsh is shared by both men, so it cannot explain the difference between their roles on its own. The added detail of a hanging drum marks רב פפא’s appointment as ראש ישיבה.

phrases.english: Some say that both of them entered a marsh,
but Rav Pappa, who hung a drum—
became head of a yeshiva,

phrases.aramaic: רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ דְּלָא תְּלֵי טַבְלָא —
phrases.english: while Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua, who did not hang a drum—
became head of the advanced students.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Retells the same appointments with a different distinction between the dreams.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the alternate account, the hanging drum distinguishes the appointment as ראש ישיבה.

steps.title: A dream includes the marsh and a sounding drum
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי reports dreaming that he entered a marsh, hung a drum, and sounded it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: I entered a marsh, hung a drum, and sounded it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי adds his own dream to the leadership stories. His dream contains the marsh and drum details from the preceding account.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The text reports what רב אשי saw, without stating an appointment in this sentence. The drum is not merely present: he also makes it sound.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: אֲנָא עֲיַילִית לְאַגְמָא
phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: I entered a marsh
and hung a drum and sounded it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: אֲנָא עֲיַילִית לְאַגְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a personal dream using the signs in the alternate account.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב אשי reports a dream of entering a marsh and sounding a hanging drum.

steps.title: Bloodletting in a dream signals forgiveness
steps.stepSummary: A reciter teaches before רב נחמן בר יצחק that dreaming of bloodletting means one’s sins are forgiven.
steps.simpleTranslation: A reciter taught before רב נחמן בר יצחק: Someone who lets blood in a dream has his sins forgiven.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new dream sign: bloodletting. The teaching gives it a favorable meaning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new case, separate from the leadership dreams. The stated outcome is forgiveness of sins.

phrases.aramaic: תָּנֵי תַּנָּא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: A reciter taught before Rav Nahman bar Yitzhak:
One who lets blood in a dream—
his sins are forgiven.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי תַּנָּא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק:
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the leadership dreams and begins a new dream interpretation.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Dreaming of bloodletting signals forgiveness of sins.

steps.title: Another teaching seems to give the opposite sign
steps.stepSummary: A cited teaching says the dreamer’s sins are arranged before him, which appears to conflict with forgiveness.
steps.simpleTranslation: But was it not taught: His sins are arranged before him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the favorable interpretation with another teaching. At first, having one’s sins arranged before him sounds unlike having them forgiven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two teachings address the same bloodletting dream. The challenge turns on what “arranged” means and whether it points to judgment rather than forgiveness.

phrases.english: But was it not taught: His sins are arranged before him!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the claim of forgiveness with a differently worded teaching about the same dream.
steps.kashyaTarget: The favorable bloodletting interpretation in step 52.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Sins being arranged before the dreamer appears to suggest scrutiny, not forgiveness.

steps.title: The sins are arranged for forgiveness
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that “arranged” means arranged in order to be forgiven.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does “arranged” mean? Arranged to be forgiven.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the apparent conflict by clarifying one word in the second teaching. The arrangement leads to forgiveness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer accepts that the sins are arranged; it changes what happens next. Both teachings can therefore describe the same favorable outcome.

phrases.english: What does ‘arranged’ mean?
Arranged to be forgiven.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies the challenged wording so that it agrees with the first teaching.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Clarifies the meaning and purpose of a word in the cited teaching.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ‘Arranged’ appeared to mean that the sins were set out for judgment.
steps.terutzMaskana: They are arranged to be forgiven.

steps.title: A snake dream is read through livelihood
steps.stepSummary: A reciter teaches before רב ששת that seeing a snake signals available livelihood, a bite signals doubled livelihood, and killing it signals lost livelihood.
steps.simpleTranslation: A reciter taught before רב ששת: Seeing a snake in a dream means livelihood is ready. If it bites him, his livelihood doubles. If he kills it, his livelihood is lost.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins another set of dream signs, this time about a snake. The teaching gives a different result for seeing, being bitten by, and killing it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The result changes with the dreamer’s encounter with the snake. The final case, killing it, will be the point רב ששת disputes.

phrases.english: A reciter taught before Rav Sheshet:

phrases.aramaic: הָרוֹאֶה נָחָשׁ בַּחֲלוֹם פַּרְנָסָתוֹ מְזוּמֶּנֶת לוֹ.
phrases.english: One who sees a snake in a dream has livelihood ready for him.
If it bit him, it doubled for him.
If he killed it, his livelihood was lost.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the resolved bloodletting dream to a new set of snake-dream cases.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Seeing, being bitten by, and killing a snake have three stated livelihood readings.

steps.title: Killing the snake receives a favorable reading
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת rejects the reciter’s negative reading of killing the snake and says it all the more indicates doubled livelihood.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת told him: All the more so, his livelihood doubled.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת disagrees with the last snake interpretation. He says killing the snake should be read as an even stronger sign of increased livelihood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He addresses only the killing case, not the earlier signs of seeing the snake or being bitten. The next line will assess his favorable claim.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said to him:
All the more so, his livelihood doubled.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן שֶׁנִּכְפְּלָה פַּרְנָסָתוֹ.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the negative interpretation of the killing case.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that killing the snake signals lost livelihood.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רב ששת proposes the opposite inference: killing it should be an even stronger favorable sign.

steps.title: The favorable reading is traced to a personal dream
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects רב ששת’s claim and notes that he himself had dreamed of killing a snake.
steps.simpleTranslation: But that is not so: רב ששת saw a snake in his dream and killed it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא does not accept רב ששת’s favorable reading. It explains why he offered it: his own dream included killing a snake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This pushes back on his interpretation of the killing case, not on every snake-dream sign. The account of his own dream helps explain why he preferred the positive reading.
steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא challenges רב ששת’s positive reading of killing the snake; it does not undo the entire list of snake signs.

phrases.english: But that is not so,

phrases.aramaic: רַב שֵׁשֶׁת הוּא דַּחֲזָא חִוְיָא בְּחֶלְמֵיהּ
phrases.english: for Rav Sheshet himself saw a snake in his dream
and killed it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא הִיא, רַב שֵׁשֶׁת הוּא דַּחֲזָא חִוְיָא בְּחֶלְמֵיהּ וְקַטְלֵיהּ.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב ששת’s favorable counter-reading and gives the personal circumstance behind it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רב ששת’s claim that killing the snake means livelihood doubles.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: His proposed reading concerns a dream he himself had, so the גמרא does not accept it as the interpretation of this case.

steps.title: All drinks are good in a dream, except wine, which can go either way
steps.stepSummary: A תנא teaches before רבי יוחנן that every kind of drink is a good sign in a dream. Wine is the exception, because for some people it is good and for others it is bad.
steps.simpleTranslation: The reciter taught before רבי יוחנן: All kinds of drinks are a good sign in a dream, except for wine. Some people drink it and it is good for them, and some drink it and it is bad for them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new dream teaching, this time about drinks. It gives a general rule and then names one exception, wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule says every drink seen in a dream is a good sign. Wine is set apart because its meaning is not fixed. It can be good or bad, depending on the person. The next step will bring פסוקים to show both sides.

keyTerms.meaning: A reciter whose job was to memorize and recite ברייתות before the חכמים

steps.confusionAlert: Here the word תנא does not mean one of the חכמי המשנה. It means a professional reciter who memorized teachings in the בית מדרש.

phrases.english: A reciter taught before Rabbi Yoḥanan:
All kinds of drinks are good for a dream
phrases.notes: Seeing them in a dream is a good sign.

phrases.english: except for wine,
there is one who drinks it and it is good for him,
and there is one who drinks it and it is bad for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the snake dream discussion to a new dream topic, drinks.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Every drink in a dream is a good sign, except wine, which can be good or bad.

steps.title: Two verses show that wine can be good or bad
steps.stepSummary: Each side of wine's double meaning is supported by a פסוק. One פסוק says wine gladdens the heart. The other links wine to people who are bitter and ruined.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some drink it and it is good for them, as it says: 'And wine gladdens the heart of man.' Some drink it and it is bad for them, as it says: 'Give strong drink to one who is perishing, and wine to the bitter of soul.'
steps.whatsHappening: The teaching now proves its claim that wine has two meanings. It brings one פסוק for the good meaning and one for the bad meaning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in תהלים shows that wine brings joy, so a wine dream can be a good sign. The פסוק in משלי shows that wine is given to those who are suffering, so a wine dream can be a bad sign. Since both ideas appear in פסוקים, wine's meaning in a dream depends on the person.

keyTerms.meaning: To one who is perishing or ruined

phrases.english: There is one who drinks it and it is good for him —
as it is stated: 'And wine gladdens the heart of man' (Psalms 104:15),
and there is one who drinks it and it is bad for him —
as it is stated: 'Give strong drink to one who is perishing,
and wine to the bitter of soul' (Proverbs 31:6).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives פסוקים to support the claim in step 58 that wine has two meanings.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that wine in a dream can be good for one person and bad for another.
steps.raayaSupportSource: תהלים קד:טו shows wine as joyful. משלי לא:ו shows wine as given to the suffering.

steps.title: For a Torah scholar, a wine dream is always good
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן tells the תנא to add a teaching: for a תלמיד חכם, dreaming of wine is always a good sign. He brings a פסוק where wisdom invites people to drink her wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said to the reciter: Teach this: For a תלמיד חכם it is always good, as it says: 'Come, eat of my bread, and drink of the wine that I have mixed.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן adds an exception to the rule that wine can go either way. For a תלמיד חכם, wine in a dream is never a bad sign.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The teaching said wine is sometimes good and sometimes bad. רבי יוחנן sets apart one type of person, the תלמיד חכם, for whom it is only good. His פסוק comes from משלי, where Torah wisdom invites people to her bread and wine. So for a Torah scholar, wine stands for Torah, which is always good.
steps.whatToRemember: Every drink in a dream is a good sign. Wine is mixed, good for some and bad for others. For a תלמיד חכם, wine is always good, because for him it stands for the wine of Torah.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוחנן is not rejecting the תנא's teaching. He keeps it and adds an exception for one kind of person.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a theme that keeps coming back in these dream סוגיות: the same dream image can mean different things depending on who the dreamer is.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said to the reciter:

phrases.aramaic: תְּנִי: תַּלְמִיד חָכָם לְעוֹלָם טוֹב לוֹ,
phrases.english: Teach: For a Torah scholar it is always good,
as it is stated: 'Come, eat of my bread,
and drink of the wine that I have mixed' (Proverbs 9:5).
phrases.notes: The speaker in the פסוק is wisdom, which is understood as Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לְתַנָּא: תְּנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds an exception to the rule that wine is mixed, set out in steps 58 and 59.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For a תלמיד חכם, a dream of wine is always a good sign.
